issues.legal_issue: A criminal complaint for wrongful withholding of company property cannot proceed where the employee’s right to occupy the accommodation arguably continued under the employment terms and the complainant had no independent right to it.
material_facts: The employee received the flat under arrangements connected with his employment, and the agreement treated the accommodation as a primary consideration for taking the employment.
The company terminated the employee’s service; he had not resigned or taken up another employment, business, profession, or vocation.
The employment agreement provided for continued rent-free accommodation in specified circumstances when the company terminated the employment.
The complainant company was not the lessee and had no right, title, or interest in the flat apart from permission granted by a related company.
The employee purchased the flat from its owner, and the company that had granted permission to occupy it had not revoked that permission or taken action against him.
A civil suit concerning possession of the flat was pending.
issues.conclusion: The High Court should not have set aside the discharge. On the facts, it could not be said that the employee had wrongfully withheld the complainant company’s property; the dispute was civil in nature. The appeal was allowed and the Magistrate’s discharge order was restored.
issues.legal_principle: Section 630 of the Companies Act applies to wrongful withholding of company property. Where the employment terms arguably preserve an employee’s right to occupy accommodation after employer-initiated termination, and the complainant company has no independent right, title, or interest in that accommodation, the facts do not establish a prima facie case of wrongful withholding. The Court also refrained from deciding the contractual issue conclusively because the civil suit was pending. No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: criminal_appeal_from_reversal_of_discharge and complaint_alleges_withholding_company_property and accommodation_was_provided_under_employment_terms and employer_terminated_employment and employment_terms_preserve_occupancy_after_employer_termination and employee_took_no_new_work and complainant_was_not_owner_or_lessee and occupant_acquired_title_to_flat and licensor_did_not_revoke_occupancy_permission

predicates.criminal_appeal_from_reversal_of_dischar: The proceeding is a criminal appeal challenging an order that reversed an accused person’s discharge.
predicates.complaint_alleges_withholding_company_pr: The complaint alleges that an employee wrongfully retained property said to belong to the employer company.
predicates.accommodation_was_provided_under_employm: The employer arranged the employee’s occupation of accommodation as part of the employment relationship.
predicates.employer_terminated_employment: The employer, rather than the employee, brought the employment to an end.
predicates.employment_terms_preserve_occupancy_afte: The employment terms provide for continued occupation of the accommodation in circumstances that include termination by the employer.
predicates.employee_took_no_new_work: The employee had not taken up another employment, business, profession, or vocation.
predicates.complainant_was_not_owner_or_lessee: The complainant company was neither the owner nor the lessee of the accommodation and had no independent property right in it.
predicates.occupant_acquired_title_to_flat: The employee acquired ownership of the accommodation from its owner.
predicates.licensor_did_not_revoke_occupancy_permis: The entity that had granted permission to occupy the accommodation had not revoked that permission or taken action against the occupant.

issues.definition: When a criminal appeal challenges the reversal of a discharge for alleged withholding of company property, and the employment arrangement arguably preserves occupancy while the complainant lacks an independent right to the accommodation, the discharge is proper where the remaining stated circumstances also apply.
